entries.title: Rapper BloodHound Q50, 22, fatally shot in Fuller Park
entries.summary: <p>The Cook County medical examiner's office identified a 22-year-old man who was fatally shot Sunday morning in Fuller Park as Mikquale Cooper of Chicago.</p><p>A manager with AMF Music Group confirmed Cooper was the rap artist who performed as BloodHound Q50.</p><p>Chicago police said Cooper was in a car around 4 a.m. in the 4200 block of South Wentworth Avenue when two cars pulled up alongside and several people in both vehicles fired shots at him, according to police.</p><p>Cooper was shot in the chest and shoulder.</p><p>He was treated by Chicago Fire Department personnel and was pronounced dead at the scene, police said.</p><p>No one has been arrested, police said.</p><p></p><p></p><p></p>

entries.title: Bears' next opponent: Vikings score 29 straight points to beat Packers 39-22
entries.summary: <p>MINNEAPOLIS — Carson Wentz has had little time to practice with Minnesota's voluminous playbook, a late arrival to the team last season who returned this year in more of a mentor role as Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy competed for the starting quarterback job in training camp.</p><p>The Vikings brought the 11th-year veteran back for emergencies like these.</p><p>Wentz came in after Murray's first-quarter concussion in his Minnesota debut and led a spirited comeback against the rival Green Bay Packers, as the Vikings scored 29 straight points to close a 39-22 victory to open the season on Sunday.</p><p>"That's why he's here," coach Kevin O'Connell said. "For him to come in and do what he did and just be part of that calming presence that allowed our team to continue playing, I can't say enough about him."</p><p>Wentz had two touchdown passes to Justin Jefferson, matching the two-time All-Pro's 2025 season total, and the pair connected on a 2-point conversion when the Vikings took their first lead at 25-22 with 6:37 remaining. Green Bay extended the drive three times with crushing defensive penalties.</p><p>"Football is a funny game," Wentz said, "but it's fun to be on this side of it."</p><p>Jordan Love, who had been brilliant against a relentlessly blitzing defense, wilted along with the rest of the team by losing a fumble on a sack and throwing an interception deep in Packers territory.</p><p>Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason each had rushing touchdowns and T.J. Hockenson caught one of the three scores thrown on a turnover-free afternoon by Wentz, who was appointed the backup to Murray ahead of the 2024 first-round draft pick McCarthy for his considerable edge in experience.</p><p>Wentz went helped the Vikings convert eight of 15 third downs and posted a 123.5 passer rating in another memorable comeback among many in five seasons under O'Connell, who has yet to win a playoff game.</p><p>"This one will stick with me for a long time," O'Connell said.</p><p>Momentum shifted when the Packers were stopped on fourth-and-1.</p><p>Love finished 21 for 42 for 387 yards and two first-half touchdowns to Christian Watson, but the two late turnovers and a 3-for-12 conversion rate on third downs loomed large as the Packers picked right up where they left off with a five-game losing streak that ended last season.</p><p>The Packers lost four times after leading in the second half by at least two possessions, including their wild card playoff collapse against the Bears, who outscored the Packers 25-6 in the fourth quarter of that game.</p><p>Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur might have mistakenly triggered this meltdown with his decision to take rookie Trey Smack's field goal off the board to set up a fourth-and-1 on an offside penalty. Love was stuffed at the line with a five-point lead, and the Vikings went the other way for the go-ahead score by Jones, the former Packers favorite who had yet to reach the end zone against his former team.</p><p>The Packers actually four defensive penalties on that drive, starting with a seemingly innocent encroachment call on Jonathan Ford.</p><p>Javon Bullard, whose injurious hit on Murray was flagged, was called for illegal contact to negate a third-down sack. Rookie Chris McClellan was penalized for a late hit on Wentz to wipe out a third-down incompletion. Then Xavier McKinney's defensive holding call erased an end-zone interception by Evan Williams, and Jones scored on the next play.</p><p>Though the penalties on McClellan and McKinney in particular were contested by the Packers, they had only themselves to blame for this collapse.</p><p>"Momentum is a strong thing," Watson said, "and we didn't respond."</p><h3>Injury report</h3><h3></h3><p>Murray seemed to be doing well after the game, O'Connell said, but the timetable for his return was unknown. ... Packers LG Aaron Banks (knee) was inactive, giving Donovan Jennings his first career start.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Packers:</b> at New York Jets on Sept. 20.</p><p><b>Vikings:</b> vs. the Bears at Soldier Field on Sept. 20.<br></p>

entries.title: A year after Operation Midway Blitz, Chicago celebrates 'strength' at the Mexican Independence Day Parade
entries.summary: <p>A year after immigration threats tempered many of Chicago's Mexican Independence Day celebrations, this year's parade aimed to bring back the full 400,000 spectators it expects to garner.</p><p>Last year's parade <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2025/09/05/mexican-independence-day-parade-little-village-immigration-ice-threat" target="_blank" >continued as planned</a>, despite fears of immigration raids during <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bearing-the-blitz" target="_blank" >Operation Midway Blitz</a>, President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement campaign targeting Chicago. But, leaders encouraged would-be attendees to do what they felt would be safest and view the parade from home, if they desired.</p><p>This year, the theme of the 55th annual event was "United We Ride: Stronger Than Ever." Held by the Little Village Chamber of Commerce, organizers said the event is one of the largest parades in the Midwest and serves as a cultural celebration and an economic driver for local businesses.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-f90000" name="image-f90000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/44fca55/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F7e%2F75%2F1df6f08c48e79b7fc74e8d2f1401%2Fmexicandayparade-260914-33-flag.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/2192851/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F7e%2F75%2F1df6f08c48e79b7fc74e8d2f1401%2Fmexicandayparade-260914-33-flag.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/c99fca9/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F7e%2F75%2F1df6f08c48e79b7fc74e8d2f1401%2Fmexicandayparade-260914-33-flag.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Participants carry large Mexican flags down 26th Street during the 55th Annual Mexican Independence Day Parade in Chicago's Little Village neighborhood on Sunday, September 13, 2026. entries.title: Man seriously wounded in South Shore shooting
entries.summary: <p>A man whose age was not immediately available was in serious condition Sunday after he was shot in the stomach in the South Shore neighborhood, Chicago police said.</p><p>Police said the man had been involved in a verbal argument with an unknown assailant who fired shots along the 2900 block of East 77th Street at about 3:15 p.m.</p><p>The victim was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center, where he was initially reported in serious condition, police said.</p><p>Area Two detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Fire fall to Revolution 2-1 at Soldier Field
entries.summary: <p>Dor Turgeman had a first-half goal and a second-half assist, Peyton Miller scored in his 50th MLS start and the New England Revolution beat the Chicago Fire 2-1 on Sunday at Soldier Field.</p><p>New England (13-8-4) moved into sole possession of third place in the Eastern Conference with 43 points, 11 behind first-place Nashville.</p><p>Chicago (11-7-6) was coming off a 1-1 draw against Inter Miami CF in front of a club-record 63,094 fans.</p><p>Turgeman opened the scoring in the 39th minute. He won a one-one-one race with Chicago defender Sam Rogers for a long ball and sent a shot past a diving Chris Brady.</p><p>Miller made it 2-0 lead in the 47th when he was left wide open at the far post to tap in a pass across the goal by Turgeman.</p><p>Maren Haile-Selassie guided in a shot into the far corner from the top of the 18-yard box in the 62nd to pull Chicago within 2-1.</p><p>New England coach Marko Mitrović returned to Chicago to face his former club after serving as an assistant coach with the Fire from 2016-19.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>New England: Hosts Orlando on Saturday.</p><p>Chicago: At Nashville on Saturday.</p>
entries.author: AP
